blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Burnaby total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Simon Fraser Hills is a hillside townhome area on the lower slope of Burnaby Mountain, in northeast Burnaby near the Lougheed Town Centre area.
The area is in the City of Burnaby and in School District 41's Cariboo Lougheed zone, which the Board lists with Burnaby Mountain Secondary and Stoney Creek Community School.
Stoney Creek has its headwaters on Burnaby Mountain and runs through neighbourhoods and parks on its way to the Brunette River, which places this hillside in the Stoney Creek watershed.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The district context for the stock is a hillside setting below Burnaby Mountain Secondary at 8800 Eastlake Drive, the secondary school the Province lists for School District 41.
Silver Creek's watershed, immediately in this part of northeast Burnaby, has headwaters on the south-facing slope of Burnaby Mountain, which is the terrain pattern the hillside complexes sit in.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A setback relaxation goes through the City's Environmental Review Committee, which reviews development applications in environmentally sensitive areas.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Stoney Creek is monitored by the Stoney Creek Environment Committee, which runs educational, monitoring and enhancement activities on the creek from Burnaby Mountain to the Brunette River.
The City collects green bin food scraps and yard waste weekly from townhomes, which matters on wooded hillside lots with heavy leaf and yard material.
The City provides weekly recycling collection for townhomes, arranged through the Solid Waste and Recycling Division for buildings that receive City service.
The temporary Cameron Community Centre is at 110-9855 Austin Avenue inside The City of Lougheed Shopping Centre during construction of the replacement facility.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: Burnaby's curbside system collects garbage every other week while recycling and green waste are collected weekly, which is the service pattern a townhome buyer should confirm for their complex.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: The Millennium Line is the rapid-transit line for this side of Burnaby, described by TransLink as running from East Vancouver through Burnaby into Port Moody and Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with the streamside check: the City's guide applies to any landowner seeking to develop within 30 metres of a stream or freshwater wetland or shoreline.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser Hills home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

11 townhomes sold in Simon Fraser Hills with a median price of $780,000 (the middle half sold between $720,000 and $922,500), taking a median of 27 days to sell at 97.5% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $551 per square foot, a median year built of 1972 and a median strata fee of $412 a month. 4 condos sold in Simon Fraser Hills, too few (5 needed) to give a typical price.
